title: Linear sections: Hilbert--Samuel bound and equality of tangent-generator degrees
statement:
Let $(V,\mathfrak l,\kappa)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $q\geq0$ and let $u_1,\ldots,u_q$ occur at distinct positions in a regular system of parameters of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak b\subseteq\mathfrak l$ be an ideal and put $D=V/\mathfrak b$, $\overline V=V/(u_1,\ldots,u_q)$, $\overline{\mathfrak b}=\mathfrak b\overline V$, and $F=\overline V/\overline{\mathfrak b}$. All quotient rings have their induced local structures. For a nonzero Noetherian local ring $(L,\mathfrak n)$ set $h_L(n)=\operatorname{length}_L(L/\mathfrak n^{n+1})$ for $n\geq0$, and put $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Then $\overline V$ is regular local and
$$h_D(n)\leq(\Lambda^q h_F)(n)\quad(n\geq0).$$
If $h_D=\Lambda^q h_F$, the quotient map induces an isomorphism
$$E(V,\mathfrak b)/(u_1^*,\ldots,u_q^*)E(V,\mathfrak b)\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ E(\overline V,\overline{\mathfrak b}),$$
where $u_i^*$ is the degree-one initial class in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V$. The images of every minimal homogeneous generating set on the left before quotienting form a minimal homogeneous generating set on the right with the same degrees; in particular $\nu^*(V,\mathfrak b)=\nu^*(\overline V,\overline{\mathfrak b})$.
For a regular local ring $(W,\mathfrak l,\kappa)$ and an ideal $\mathfrak c\subseteq\mathfrak l$, write $E(W,\mathfrak c)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}W\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l/\mathfrak c}(W/\mathfrak c))$. The sequence $\nu^*(W,\mathfrak c)$ contains $d\geq1$ with multiplicity $\dim_\kappa(E_d/\sum_{j=1}^d(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}W)_jE_{d-j})$, sorted increasingly and padded by infinitely many $\infty$'s.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), Propositions 5--6, pp.157--159, Lemma 7, p.160, and the first part of Remark (12.2), p.167; iterated linear sections. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this complete comparison.

proof.text: Complete the displayed $u_i$ to a regular system of parameters and permute it so they come first. Put $R_i=V/(u_1,\ldots,u_i)$, $J_i=\mathfrak bR_i$, $D_i=R_i/J_i$, and denote their maximal ideals by $\mathfrak l_i$ and $\mathfrak m_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $R_i$ is regular local and the remaining parameter images form a regular system of parameters. In particular $R_q=\overline V$. The ideals $J_i$ are contained in $\mathfrak l_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian], all $D_i$ are nonzero Noetherian local rings, and their common residue field is $\kappa$. Here $D_0=D$, $D_q=F$ and $D_{i+1}=D_i/u_{i+1}D_i$.

proof.text: All lengths used below are finite by [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge], applied to each $D_i$. For a quotient $L\twoheadrightarrow B$ and a $B$-module $M$, the $L$-submodules of $M$ are exactly its $B$-submodules: every $B$ scalar lifts to $L$. Thus their chains, and hence lengths, coincide by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. We may compute all lengths for $B=D_{i+1}$ over $L=D_i$. A finite-length module has length zero exactly when it is zero: a nonzero module has the strict chain $0\subsetneq M$.

proof.text: Fix $i<q$, write $L=D_i$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_i$, $z=u_{i+1}$ in $L$, and $B=L/zL$. For $n\ge0$ multiplication induces $L/\mathfrak m^n\xrightarrow{z}L/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$, with kernel $K_n=(\mathfrak m^{n+1}:z)/\mathfrak m^n$ and cokernel $B/(\mathfrak m B)^{n+1}$. Indeed $z\mathfrak m^n\subseteq\mathfrak m^{n+1}$, and the image is $(zL+\mathfrak m^{n+1})/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] to the kernel-image sequence and the image-cokernel sequence. With $h_L(-1)=0$ this gives $h_L(n)=h_L(n-1)+h_B(n)-\operatorname{length}_L K_n$. Summing from $0$ to $n$ gives $h_L(n)=(\Lambda h_B)(n)-\sum_{a=0}^n\operatorname{length}_L K_a\le(\Lambda h_B)(n)$. At $n=0$, $L/\mathfrak m^0=0$ and $K_0=0$, so the same formula applies.

proof.text: Set $h_i=h_{D_i}$. The previous inequality and preservation of pointwise inequalities by finite sums give $h_0\le\Lambda h_1\le\cdots\le\Lambda^q h_q$, proving the bound. Suppose its endpoints agree. For $0\le i<q$ put $\delta_i=\Lambda h_{i+1}-h_i\ge0$. The difference of the two adjacent terms of this chain is $\Lambda^i\delta_i$, and is zero because both lie between the equal endpoints. For every $n$, $(\Lambda^i\delta_i)(n)\ge\delta_i(n)$: prove this by induction on $i$, since the last summand in a cumulative sum is its value at $n$. Hence $\delta_i=0$, so equality holds at each single section. Step 3 now gives $\sum_{a=0}^n\operatorname{length}K_a=0$, whence every $K_n=0$.

proof.text: For the fixed section of step 3, vanishing of $K_n$ says $(\mathfrak m^{n+1}:z)=\mathfrak m^n$ for every $n\ge0$. Let $A=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}L$ and let $t\in A_1$ be the class of $z$. If $a\in\mathfrak m^r$ represents a class killed by $t$, then $za\in\mathfrak m^{r+2}$; the colon identity for $n=r+1$ gives $a\in\mathfrak m^{r+1}$. Thus multiplication by $t$ is injective on each degree, and on their direct sum. This uses precisely the multiplication formula in [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring].

proof.text: The map $A\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m B}B$ is surjective in every degree, since $(\mathfrak m B)^r$ is the image of $\mathfrak m^r$. For $r\ge1$ an element of its degree-$r$ kernel has a representative $a\in\mathfrak m^r$ of the form $a=zb+c$, $c\in\mathfrak m^{r+1}$. Then $zb\in\mathfrak m^r$, so the colon identity with $n=r-1$ gives $b\in\mathfrak m^{r-1}$; its class is therefore $t[b]$. Conversely every such product maps to zero. In degree zero the map is the identity of the residue field. This proves the canonical graded isomorphism $A/tA\simeq\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m B}B$, without appealing to an unrecorded initial-ideal comparison.

proof.text: For this section put $R=R_i$, $S=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l_i}R$, $I=E(R_i,J_i)$, and $t=u_{i+1}^*\in S_1$. The parameter $u_{i+1}$ is nonzero and has order one. By [lem-sfb-regular-hypersurface-initial-form], $S$ is a polynomial algebra in the remaining parameter classes and $S/tS\simeq\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l_{i+1}}R_{i+1}$ canonically. The quotient $S\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m_i}D_i=A$ is surjective: a degree-$r$ class in the latter lifts to $\mathfrak l_i^r$. Its kernel is $I$ by definition, so $A=S/I$. Steps 5--6 show that $t$ acts injectively on $S/I$ and that $S/(I+tS)\simeq\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m_{i+1}}D_{i+1}$.

proof.text: If $tb\in I$ for $b\in S$, then injectivity of $t$ on $S/I$ gives $b\in I$. Consequently $I\cap tS=tI$. The map $I\to S/tS$ has kernel $tI$ and image the kernel of $S/tS\to S/(I+tS)$. By the canonical identifications in step 7 this latter kernel is exactly $I'=E(R_{i+1},J_{i+1})$. Thus $I/tI\simeq I'$ as graded modules. Iterating these isomorphisms gives the asserted $E(V,\mathfrak b)/(u_1^*,\ldots,u_q^*)E(V,\mathfrak b)\simeq E(\overline V,\overline{\mathfrak b})$: at stage $i$ the ambient graded map is the quotient by the first $i$ parameter classes, so the successive module quotients are the quotient by their sum.

proof.text: Write $S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d$ and $S'=S/tS$. Under step 8, $S'_+I'$ is the image of $S_+I$. Since $tI\subseteq S_+I$, reduction induces a degree-preserving vector-space isomorphism $I/S_+I\simeq I'/S'_+I'$. Images of a given homogeneous generating family generate $I'$. To check minimality, recall the elementary graded criterion: for any homogeneous generating family $g_j$ of a nonnegatively graded ideal $M$, it is minimal exactly when the classes of $g_j$ form a basis of $M/S_+M$. Independence follows because a homogeneous dependence of degree $d$ expresses one degree-$d$ generator using the others plus positive-degree multiples of generators of smaller degree; these expressions make that generator redundant. Conversely redundancy gives such a dependence by taking constant terms in an expression in the other generators. Spanning follows from generation. For this argument take the degree-$d$ parts of each expression; positive-degree coefficients only involve generators of degree strictly below $d$. Applying the criterion to the displayed isomorphism proves that every minimal homogeneous generating family remains minimal, no image vanishes, and all its degrees are unchanged.

proof.text: In degree $d$, $(S_+I)_d=\sum_{j=1}^dS_jI_{d-j}$. The degree-preserving isomorphism of step 9 therefore equates exactly the dimensions defining the multiplicities in $\nu^*$, for every $d\ge1$. Sorting and padding by $\infty$ gives the asserted equality of sequences. Iterate step 9 for the given generating family through all $q$ sections. If $q=0$, all maps are identities and the inequality is equality. If $I=0$, the empty minimal generating family and the all-$\infty$ sequence are covered by the same argument.
